# CPython `re` semantics — a differential spec for a future tier-1 engine

**2026-08-31.** Generated by four agents that ran every case below against the
real CPython 3.11 on this container and kept the ones where a naive backtracker
plausibly diverges. Each is an executable input/output pair, so this file is a
test corpus, not prose.

**Why it is here rather than implemented.** `re` is the top row of
`conformance --plan` at 185 programs, and implementing it in tier 1 was this
iteration's plan — until routing measurement showed those programs are already
answered correctly by **lypning-mp** at a 0.36 ms spawn, not by CPython at
11 ms. `modules.rs` had said so all along: "`re` is deliberately ABSENT ... 
lypning-mp already has one, so `import re` is a routing decision rather than a
gap to fill here." The spec is kept because the day tier 1 *does* want `re` —
for the 6 programs that reach CPython, or to stop paying the mp spawn — this is
the boundary it has to match, already measured.

**How to use it.** Every `expr => value` line is ground truth from CPython 3.11
on 2026-08-31. Re-run them before trusting them (invariant 3): a future CPython
may differ, and `re.split` on empty matches already changed once, in 3.7.

---

Verified against CPython 3.11.15 (Linux x86-64, run 2026-08-31); every pair below is a literal transcript, not recollection. Scratch probes are at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-lypning/13f3494a-8f12-5202-84b8-45addf9cef2c/scratchpad/p1.py` … `pa.py`.

# A. Bracket parsing — what counts as a literal

`]` immediately after `[` or after `[^` is a **literal**, not the terminator. Everywhere else it terminates.

- `re.findall(r'[]]', 'a]b')` → `[']']`
- `re.findall(r'[]a]', 'a]b')` → `['a', ']']`
- `re.findall(r'[^]]', 'a]b')` → `['a', 'b']`
- `re.findall(r'[^]a]', 'a]b')` → `['b']`
- `re.findall(r'[]]]', 'a]]b')` → `[']]']`  (class `[]]` then a literal `]`)
- `re.findall(r'[a]]', 'a]b')` → `['a]']`  (class `[a]` then literal `]`)
- `re.findall(r'[]', 'a]b')` → `re.error: unterminated character set at position 0`
- `re.findall(r'[^]', 'a')` → `re.error: unterminated character set at position 0`
- `re.findall(r'[a', 'a')` → `re.error: unterminated character set at position 0`

`^` is negation only in position 0; elsewhere it is a literal, and it is also a literal member of a negated class if repeated.

- `re.findall(r'[a^]', '^a')` → `['^', 'a']`
- `re.findall(r'[\^a]', '^a')` → `['^', 'a']`
- `re.findall(r'[^^]', '^a')` → `['a']`
- `re.findall(r'[$^]', 'a$^')` → `['$', '^']`

Regex metacharacters are inert inside a class; `[` is a literal (with a warning, see §J); a POSIX class is silently *not* one.

- `re.findall(r'[.]', 'a.b')` → `['.']`
- `re.findall(r'[*+?]', 'a*+?')` → `['*', '+', '?']`
- `re.findall(r'[(|)]', 'a(|)')` → `['(', '|', ')']`
- `re.findall(r'[{}]', 'a{}')` → `['{', '}']`
- `re.findall(r'[[]', 'a[b')` → `['[']` plus `FutureWarning: Possible nested set at position 1` on stderr
- `re.findall(r'[[:alpha:]]', 'ab[]:alph')` → `['[]']` — this is the set `{[ : a l p h}` followed by a literal `]`, **not** a POSIX class. A naive engine that either implements POSIX classes or errors on them is wrong; CPython matches `'[]'` here.

# B. Ranges

`-` is a literal when first, when last, or immediately after a completed range. A range whose endpoint is a class-escape, or whose start > end, is a hard error.

- `re.findall(r'[-a]', 'a-b')` → `['a', '-']`
- `re.findall(r'[a-]', 'a-b')` → `['a', '-']`
- `re.findall(r'[^-a]', 'a-b')` → `['b']`
- `re.findall(r'[a\-c]', 'abc-')` → `['a', 'c', '-']`  (escaped `-` is literal; `b` is **not** in the class)
- `re.findall(r'[a-c-e]', 'abcde-')` → `['a', 'b', 'c', 'e', '-']`  (`a-c`, then literal `-`, then literal `e`; `d` is not in it)
- `re.findall(r'[--0]', ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32,65)))` → `['-', '.', '/', '0']`  (range U+002D..U+0030; no warning, `-` here is a range *start*)
- `re.findall(r'[]-a]', ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x58,0x62)))` → `[']', '^', '_', '`', 'a']`  (leading `]` is a literal *and* a range start: U+005D..U+0061)
- `re.findall(r'[Z-\\]', 'XYZ[\\]')` → `['Z', '[', '\\']`
- `re.findall(r'[a-a]', 'abc')` → `['a']`
- `re.findall(r'[z-a]', 'abc')` → `re.error: bad character range z-a at position 1`
- `re.findall(r'[\d-a]', '1-a')` → `re.error: bad character range \d-a at position 1`
- `re.findall(r'[a-\d]', '1-a')` → `re.error: bad character range a-\d at position 1`
- `re.findall(r'[a--b]', 'x')` → `re.error: bad character range a-- at position 1` (preceded by a FutureWarning)

Note the asymmetry: `[a-c-e]` is legal because the trailing `-` follows a *completed* range, while `[\d-a]` is illegal because `\d` cannot be a range endpoint. An engine that treats "`-` after a class-escape" as literal will silently accept `[\d-a]` and match `-`; CPython raises.

# C. Escapes inside a class

Accepted and their exact values:

- `re.findall(r'[\n\t]', 'a\n\tb')` → `['\n', '\t']`
- `re.findall(r'[\a\f\v\r]', '\a\f\v\r x')` → `['\x07', '\x0c', '\x0b', '\r']`
- `re.findall(r'[\\]', 'a\\b')` → `['\\']`
- `re.findall(r'[\]]', 'a]b')` → `[']']`
- `re.findall(r'[\^a]', '^a')` → `['^', 'a']`
- `re.findall(r'[\-]', 'a-b')` → `['-']`
- **`re.findall(r'[\b]', 'a\bb')` → `['\x08']`** — inside a class `\b` is BACKSPACE U+0008, not a word boundary. Outside a class it is the boundary assertion. Same two characters, two completely different meanings.
- `re.findall(r'[\x41]', 'Aa')` → `['A']`
- `re.findall(r'[\101]', 'Aa')` → `['A']` (octal)
- `re.findall(r'[\0]', 'A\0')` → `['\x00']`
- `re.findall(r'[\xff]', 'ÿ')` → `['ÿ']`
- `re.findall(r'[\x80-\xff]+', 'naïve')` → `['ï']` — for a **str** pattern these are codepoints, not bytes; `ï` is U+00EF and matches as one character.
- `re.findall(r'[\N{DEGREE SIGN}]', 'a°')` → `['°']`; `\uXXXX` and `\UXXXXXXXX` likewise work in str patterns.
- `re.findall(r'[\d]', '1a')` → `['1']`; `[\w]`, `[\s]`, `[\D]`, `[\W]`, `[\S]` all legal inside a class.
- `re.findall(r'[\D\d]', 'a1')` → `['a', '1']` (union — matches everything)
- `re.findall(r'[\w\W]', 'a\n')` → `['a', '\n']`

Hard errors inside a class:

- `re.findall(r'[\A]', 'A a')` → `re.error: bad escape \A at position 1`
- `re.findall(r'[\Z]', 'Z z')` → `re.error: bad escape \Z at position 1`
- `re.findall(r'[\q]', 'q')` → `re.error: bad escape \q at position 1`
- `re.findall(r'[\e]', 'e')` → `re.error: bad escape \e at position 1`
- `re.findall(r'[\8]', '8')` → `re.error: bad escape \8 at position 1`

The rule is: unknown escapes of ASCII letters and digits are errors; there is no "backslash before an unknown char means the char itself" fallback in patterns. An engine that silently treats `[\q]` as `q` produces a MISMATCH against a traceback.

# D. Negated classes and newline

A negated class **does** match `\n`; only `.` does not (without DOTALL). This is the single most common naive-engine bug in this area, because implementers reuse the dot's "not newline" mask.

- `re.findall(r'[^a]', 'a\nb')` → `['\n', 'b']`
- `re.findall(r'.', 'a\nb')` → `['a', 'b']`
- `re.findall(r'[^\d]', '1\n2')` → `['\n']`
- `re.findall(r'[\W]', 'a\nb ')` → `['\n', ' ']`
- `re.findall(r'[^a]*', '\n\n')` → `['\n\n', '']`
- `re.sub(r'[^a]', 'X', 'a\nb')` → `'aXX'`
- `re.split(r'[^a]+', 'x\nay\nz')` → `['', 'a', '']`

# E. `\d` `\w` `\s` `\b` — Unicode is the default for str patterns

Exact semantics, established by a full 0..0x10FFFF sweep on this build:

- `\w` ≡ `ch.isalnum() or ch == '_'` — **133,548** codepoints (0 disagreements over the whole range).
- `\d` ≡ Unicode general category **Nd** — **660** codepoints. It is *not* `str.isdigit()`: 128 codepoints disagree (`²` `³` `¹`, ETHIOPIC DIGIT ONE U+1369, …).
- `\s` ≡ `ch.isspace()` — **29** codepoints: `\t \n \v \f \r` U+001C U+001D U+001E U+001F `' '` U+0085 U+00A0 U+1680 U+2000–U+200A U+2028 U+2029 U+202F U+205F U+3000.

Concrete non-ASCII that `\w` matches (all `re.findall(r'\w+', …)` → the whole string):

`é` U+00E9, `ï`, `Ω` U+03A9, `日本語`, `Кириллица`, `ﬁ` U+FB01 LATIN SMALL LIGATURE FI, `ª` U+00AA, `µ` U+00B5 MICRO SIGN, `ß`, `ı` U+0131, `İ` U+0130, `ſ` U+017F, `²` U+00B2, `³`, `¹`, `½` U+00BD, `¾`, `⅓` U+2153, `Ⅻ` U+216B ROMAN NUMERAL TWELVE, `Ⅰ` U+2160, `〇` U+3007, `⑤` U+2464 CIRCLED DIGIT FIVE, `⓪` U+24EA, `⁴` U+2074 SUPERSCRIPT FOUR, `₄` U+2084 SUBSCRIPT FOUR, `４` U+FF14, `ａ` U+FF41, `ʼ` U+02BC MODIFIER LETTER APOSTROPHE, `ʻ` U+02BB.

Concrete non-ASCII that `\d` matches: `٤` U+0664 ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT FOUR, `۵` U+06F5, `०` U+0966 DEVANAGARI DIGIT ZERO, `९` U+096F, `๑` U+0E51 THAI DIGIT ONE, `４` U+FF14 FULLWIDTH DIGIT FOUR.

Concrete non-ASCII that `\w` matches but `\d` does **not**, despite looking numeric: `²` `³` `¹` `½` `¾` `⅓` `Ⅻ` `⁴` `₄` `⑤` `⓪` `〇`.

Concrete characters that are `\w`=False and worth a test because a naive table gets them wrong: `́` U+0301 COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT (`\w` False — so NFD `'cafe\u0301'` is **not** one `\w+` run: `re.findall(r'\w+','cafe\u0301')` → `['cafe']`, while NFC `re.findall(r'\w+','café')` → `['café']`), `·` U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT, `-` U+002D.

Concrete `\s` traps:

- `re.findall(r'\s', '\x1c')` → `['\x1c']` — **U+001C–U+001F are ASCII and they are `\s`.** An engine whose whitespace set is `[ \t\n\r\f\v]` is wrong on pure-ASCII input. `re.sub(r'\s+', '_', 'a\x1cb')` → `'a_b'`; `re.split(r'\s+', 'a\x1cb')` → `['a','b']`; `re.findall(r'[^\s]+', 'a\x1cb')` → `['a','b']`.
- `re.split(r'\s+', 'a\xa0b')` → `['a', 'b']` (NBSP is `\s`); `re.findall(r'\S+', 'a\xa0b')` → `['a', 'b']`.
- `re.findall(r'\s', '\u200b')` → `[]` — ZERO WIDTH SPACE is **not** `\s`. Same for `\ufeff` (BOM).
- `re.findall(r'\s', '\u0085')` → `['\x85']` (NEL), `'\u3000'`, `'\u1680'`, `'\u202f'`, `'\u205f'` all `\s`.

`\b`/`\B` inherit all of this:

- `re.sub(r'\b', '|', 'café')` → `'|café|'`
- `re.sub(r'\b', '|', 'café', flags=re.A)` → `'|caf|é'`
- `re.findall(r'\b\w+\b', 'café x')` → `['café', 'x']`
- `re.findall(r'\b', 'é')` → `['', '']`

Idioms your corpus will contain:

- `re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', 'a1_é')` → `['a', 'é']`
- `re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', 'Ⅻ½²')` → `['Ⅻ½²']` (all three are `\w` and none is `\d`)
- `re.sub(r'[^\w\s]', '', 'a,b é!')` → `'ab é'`
- `re.split(r'\W+', 'naïve word')` → `['naïve', 'word']` — an ASCII engine gives `['na', 've', 'word']`.

For **bytes** patterns the ASCII sets are correct and simple: `\s` on bytes is exactly `{0x09,0x0a,0x0b,0x0c,0x0d,0x20}` (no `\x1c`!), `\w` is exactly `[0-9A-Za-z_]`, `\d` is `[0-9]`. `re.findall(rb'\w+', 'naïve'.encode())` → `[b'na', b've']`. So the bytes path is safe for an ASCII engine and the str path is not — that distinction is the cleanest place to draw the supported/refused line.

# F. IGNORECASE

Under `re.I` with a str pattern, exactly **four** non-ASCII codepoints are reachable from an ASCII pattern (verified by sweeping all of 0..0x10FFFF against `[\x00-\x7f]` with `re.I`):

| char | name | matched by ASCII |
|---|---|---|
| U+0130 `İ` | LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE | `I`, `i` |
| U+0131 `ı` | LATIN SMALL LETTER DOTLESS I | `I`, `i` |
| U+017F `ſ` | LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S | `S`, `s` |
| U+212A `K` | KELVIN SIGN | `K`, `k` |

Pairs:

- `re.findall(r'[a-z]', '\u212a', re.I)` → `['K']` — an ASCII range matching a non-ASCII char.
- `re.findall(r'[a-z]+', 'K\u212a\u017fs', re.I)` → `['KK\u017fs']` (one run of four)
- `re.findall(r's', '\u017f', re.I)` → `['\u017f']`; `re.findall('\u017f', 's', re.I)` → `['s']` (symmetric)
- `re.findall(r'i', '\u0130', re.I)` → `['\u0130']`; `re.findall(r'I', '\u0131', re.I)` → `['\u0131']`
- `re.findall(r'[A-Z]', '\u017f', re.I)` → `['\u017f']`
- `re.findall(r'[^a-z]', '\u212a', re.I)` → `[]` — negation is computed *after* folding, so Kelvin is excluded from `[^a-z]`.
- `re.findall(r'[^a-z]+', '\u212a k1', re.I)` → `[' ', '1']`
- `re.findall(r'[0-9a-f]', '\u212a\u017f', re.I)` → `[]` (folds land outside the range — the folding is per-character, not a blanket "add the other case of the whole range")
- `re.findall(r'[a-f]+', 'ABCDEFG', re.I)` → `['ABCDEF']`
- `re.findall(r'[A-_]', 'a', re.I)` → `['a']` — the range U+0041..U+005F contains `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `_` as well as A–Z, and folding still pulls in lowercase.
- `re.sub(r'[a-z]', 'X', 'KELVIN \u212a', flags=re.I)` → `'XXXXXX X'`
- `re.split(r'[s]', 'ma\u017fse', flags=re.I)` → `['ma', '', 'e']`
- `re.subn(r'[s]+', 'S', '\u017fs', flags=re.I)` → `('S', 1)`
- With `re.A` these all revert: `re.findall(r'[a-z]', '\u212a', re.I|re.A)` → `[]`.

Non-ASCII case folding (simple, single-codepoint; no multi-char expansions):

- `re.findall('[a-\xff]', 'É', re.I)` → `['É']`
- `re.findall('é', 'É', re.I)` → `['É']`
- `re.findall('[à-ÿ]+', 'ÀÉÞ', re.I)` → `['ÀÉÞ']`
- `re.findall('µ', 'μ', re.I)` → `['μ']` (MICRO SIGN U+00B5 ≡ GREEK SMALL MU U+03BC)
- `re.findall('Ω', 'ω', re.I)` → `['ω']` (OHM SIGN U+2126 folds to omega)
- `re.findall('σ', 'ς', re.I)` → `['ς']`; `re.findall('Σ', 'ς', re.I)` → `['ς']` (all three sigmas equivalent)
- `re.findall('ẞ', 'ß', re.I)` → `['ß']`
- `re.findall('ǅ', 'Ǆ', re.I)` → `['Ǆ']` and `re.findall('ǆ', 'Ǆ', re.I)` → `['Ǆ']` (all three DZ forms equivalent)
- `re.findall('\u0345', 'ι', re.I)` → `['ι']` (COMBINING GREEK YPOGEGRAMMENI ≡ iota)

And what `re.I` does **not** do — full case folding is absent, so these are all empty:

- `re.findall('ß', 'SS', re.I)` → `[]`
- `re.findall('ﬀ', 'FF', re.I)` → `[]`
- `re.findall(r'\w', '\u0130', re.A)` → `[]`

# G. `re.escape`

3.7+ escapes exactly this set and nothing else: `\t \n \x0b \x0c \r`, space, `#`, `$`, `&`, `(`, `)`, `*`, `+`, `-`, `.`, `?`, `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `{`, `|`, `}`, `~`. Note what is **not** escaped: `!` `"` `'` `,` `/` `:` `;` `<` `=` `>` `@` `` ` `` `_` `%`, all ASCII letters and digits, `\x00`–`\x08`, `\x0e`–`\x1f`, `\x7f`, and every non-ASCII codepoint.

- `re.escape('a-b')` → `'a\\-b'`
- `re.escape(' ')` → `'\\ '`
- `re.escape('\n')` → `'\\\n'` — a backslash followed by a **real newline byte**, not the two characters `\` `n`. Printing it gives a backslash then a line break.
- `re.escape('naïve°')` → `'naïve°'` (unchanged)
- `re.escape('\xa0')` → `'\xa0'` (unchanged — NBSP is not escaped even though it is `\s`)
- `re.escape('')` → `''`
- `re.escape(b'a-b ')` → `b'a\\-b\\ '`; `re.escape('é'.encode())` → `b'\xc3\xa9\\ \\-'` for `b'\xc3\xa9 -'`

Round-trip test worth having: `re.findall(re.escape(s), s)` must be `[s]` for `s` over the ASCII range and for a handful of non-ASCII.

# H. Replacement-template escapes for `sub`/`subn`

The template is a *different* grammar from the pattern; this is where hand-rolled engines that reuse the pattern escape table go wrong.

- `re.sub(r'a', r'\n', 'a')` → `'\n'`; `\t \r \f \v \a` likewise
- `re.sub(r'a', r'\b', 'a')` → `'\x08'`
- `re.sub(r'a', r'\\', 'a')` → `'\\'`
- `re.sub(r'a', r'\0', 'a')` → `'\x00'`; `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\101', 'a')` → `'A'` (octal); `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\1', 'a')` → `'a'`; `re.sub(r'a', r'\g<0>!', 'a')` → `'a!'`
- `re.sub(r'a', r'\x41', 'a')` → `re.error: bad escape \x at position 0` — `\x` is legal in a *pattern* and illegal in a *template*.
- `re.sub(r'a', r'\N{DEGREE SIGN}', 'a')` → `re.error: bad escape \N at position 0` — same asymmetry.
- `re.sub(r'a', r'\d', 'a')` → `re.error: bad escape \d at position 0`; same for `\s`, `\w`, `\A`, `\q`
- `re.sub(r'a', '\\8', 'a')` → `re.error: invalid group reference 8 at position 1`
- **`re.sub(r'(a)', r'\-', 'a')` → `'\\-'`** and `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\ ', 'a')` → `'\\ '` — an unknown escape of a *non-letter* keeps the backslash. Only ASCII letters/digits raise. So `re.sub(r'x', re.escape('a-b'), 'x')` → `'a\\-b'`, with the backslash surviving into the output.

# I. Empty matches (classes produce these constantly)

Since 3.7, an empty match adjacent to a previous match is allowed and advances by one.

- `re.findall(r'[^a]*', 'ba')` → `['b', '', '']`
- `re.sub(r'[^a]*', '-', 'ba')` → `'--a-'`
- `re.split(r'[^a]*', 'ba')` → `['', '', 'a', '']`
- `re.split(r'x*', 'axbxc')` → `['', 'a', '', 'b', '', 'c', '']`
- `re.split(r'[^a]+', 'xaybz')` → `['', 'a', '']`
- `re.split(r'([,;])', 'a,b;c')` → `['a', ',', 'b', ';', 'c']`
- `re.split(r'[,;]', 'a,b;c', maxsplit=1)` → `['a', 'b;c']`

# J. FutureWarning is stderr noise you cannot reproduce

`--`, `&&`, `~~`, `||`, and a nested `[` inside a set emit a `FutureWarning` on stderr at compile time — and the warning registry dedupes by message text and source line, so whether it appears depends on what the program compiled *earlier*.

- `re.findall(r'[a&&b]', 'ab&')` → `['a','b','&','a']` + `FutureWarning: Possible set intersection at position 2`
- `re.findall(r'[a||b]', …)` → `Possible set union at position 2`; `[a~~b]` → `Possible set symmetric difference`; `[[a]]` → `Possible nested set at position 1`
- `re.findall(r'[+--]', '+,-. ')` → `['+', ',', '-']` + `Possible set difference at position 2`
- `re.findall(r'[!--]', …)` → same shape, **no warning**, because `[+--]` already emitted that exact message from that line
- `re.compile('[a--b]')` → warns *and then* raises `re.error: bad character range a--`
- `re.findall(r'[--0]', …)` → `['-','.','/','0']`, no warning (leading `-` is a range start)

# K. What an ASCII-only engine must REFUSE

Refuse at pattern-parse (or call) time — before matching, so exit 90 lands cleanly:

1. **Any `\d` `\w` `\s` `\D` `\W` `\S` `\b` `\B` in a str pattern** — inside or outside a class — unless you ship the real Unicode tables. There is no ASCII-safe shortcut: even a pure-ASCII *subject* breaks on U+001C–U+001F for `\s`. If you want a narrow supported slice, allow these only for `bytes` patterns, where the ASCII definitions are exact.
2. **Any non-ASCII codepoint anywhere in the pattern** (literal, class member, range endpoint, `\uXXXX`, `\UXXXXXXXX`, `\N{…}`, `\x80`–`\xff` in a str pattern), and any non-ASCII in the *subject* if you match `.` or a negated class over it — a UTF-8-byte-oriented engine will split `ï` into two "characters" and `re.findall(r'.', 'naïve')` will return 6 items instead of 5.
3. **`re.IGNORECASE`** in any form, unless you also refuse `s S k K i I` and all non-ASCII — the four folds (U+0130, U+0131, U+017F, U+212A) plus every non-ASCII pair are unreachable without tables. `[a-z]` matching U+212A is exactly the kind of silent disagreement invariant 1 is about.
4. **Any pattern containing `--`, `&&`, `~~`, `||` inside a class, or `[` inside a class** — you cannot reproduce CPython's registry-dependent stderr warnings.
5. **`\N{…}`, `\uXXXX`, `\UXXXXXXXX`** even when the named char is ASCII, unless you implement the full name table.
6. **`re.ASCII` / `re.A`, `re.LOCALE`, `re.UNICODE`, `re.VERBOSE`, `re.DOTALL`, `re.MULTILINE`** flags passed as the `flags=` argument to findall/sub/subn/split — same reasoning as inline flags. (`re.A` would actually make your ASCII engine *correct*, so it is the one flag worth supporting deliberately; but it must be recognised, not ignored.)
7. **Anything CPython raises `re.error` on**: reversed ranges, `\d` as a range endpoint, `[\A]`/`[\q]`/`[\8]`, unterminated sets, bad template escapes. Refusing is far cheaper than reproducing `re.error: bad character range \d-a at position 1` and its traceback byte-for-byte.

What you can safely support in ASCII: literal chars, `.` (as "not `\n`", over codepoints), classes with `]`-first / `-`-edge / `^` rules from §A–B, `\n \t \r \f \v \a \b(=U+0008 in class) \\ \] \^ \- \xNN \NNN \0` inside classes, `^ $ \A \Z` anchors, groups, alternation, quantifiers — all restricted to an all-ASCII pattern *and* an all-ASCII subject, with `\w \d \s \b` reserved for the bytes path.

---

All pairs below were executed on CPython 3.11.15 (`/usr/bin/python3.11`, this container, 2026-08-31). Everything shown as `expr => value` is verbatim ground truth from that run; I ran ~300 cases and kept the ones where a naive backtracker plausibly diverges. Scripts and case lists are at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-lypning/13f3494a-8f12-5202-84b8-45addf9cef2c/scratchpad/cases.txt`, `cases2.txt`, `cases3.txt`, `cases4.txt` with runners `run.py`..`run4.py` — they take one expression per line and print `expr => repr`, so they drop straight into a differential harness.

## A. Leftmost-first, not leftmost-longest

The scan position dominates; only at a fixed start position does alternative order decide. A DFA/POSIX-longest implementation gets every one of these wrong.

    re.findall(r'a|ab', 'ab')            => ['a']
    re.findall(r'ab|a', 'ab')            => ['ab']
    re.findall(r'a|ab|abc', 'abc')       => ['a']
    re.findall(r'foo|foobar', 'foobar')  => ['foo']
    re.sub(r'a|ab', 'X', 'ab')           => 'Xb'
    re.split(r'a|ab', 'zabz')            => ['z', 'bz']
    re.findall(r'b|a', 'ab')             => ['a', 'b']        # leftmost beats order
    re.findall(r'\d+|\w+', 'ab12')       => ['ab12']          # \w+ wins by position, not order
    re.findall(r'[0-9]+|[a-z]+', 'ab12') => ['ab', '12']

Backtracking must be able to re-enter an earlier alternative after a later element fails, and the group spans must reflect the branch that finally succeeded:

    re.findall(r'(a|ab)(c|bcd)', 'abcd')          => [('a', 'bcd')]   # NOT ('ab','cd')
    re.findall(r'(?:ab|a)(?:c|bc)', 'abc')        => ['abc']
    re.findall(r'(?:a|ab)(?:c|bcd)(?:d|)', 'abcd')=> ['abcd']
    re.findall(r'(?:a|ab)+c', 'ababc')            => ['ababc']
    re.findall(r'(?:a|ab)$', 'ab')                => ['ab']
    re.findall(r'(?:a|ab)\Z', 'ab')               => ['ab']

Empty alternation branches are legal and are tried in written order:

    re.findall(r'|a', 'ab')      => ['', 'a', '', '']
    re.findall(r'x|', 'ab')      => ['', '', '']
    re.findall(r'a|', 'aa')      => ['a', 'a', '']
    re.sub(r'a|', '-', 'aa')     => '---'
    re.findall(r'(a|)', 'ba')    => ['', 'a', '']
    re.findall(r'(|a)b', 'ab')   => ['a']          # empty branch first, then backtrack to 'a'
    re.findall(r'(a||b)c', 'bc') => ['b']
    re.findall(r'(?:|a)*', 'aa') => ['', 'a', '', 'a', '']
    re.findall(r'(?:a|)+', 'aa') => ['aa', '']

## B. Greedy vs lazy backtracking order

    re.findall(r'<.*>', '<a><b>')    => ['<a><b>']
    re.findall(r'<.*?>', '<a><b>')   => ['<a>', '<b>']
    re.findall(r'".*"', '"a" "b"')   => ['"a" "b"']
    re.findall(r'".*?"', '"a" "b"')  => ['"a"', '"b"']
    re.findall(r'.*b', 'abcb')       => ['abcb']
    re.findall(r'.*?b', 'abcb')      => ['ab', 'cb']
    re.findall(r'a+', 'aaa')         => ['aaa']
    re.findall(r'a+?', 'aaa')        => ['a', 'a', 'a']
    re.sub(r'a+?', '-', 'aaa')       => '---'
    re.split(r'a+?', 'xaaay')        => ['x', '', '', 'y']
    re.findall(r'a*?', 'aaa')        => ['', 'a', '', 'a', '', 'a', '']
    re.findall(r'a??', 'aaa')        => ['', 'a', '', 'a', '', 'a', '']
    re.findall(r'x{2,3}', 'xxxx')    => ['xxx']
    re.findall(r'x{2,3}?', 'xxxx')   => ['xx', 'xx']
    re.findall(r'a{2,}?', 'aaaa')    => ['aa', 'aa']
    re.findall(r'a{2,3}?b', 'aaab')  => ['aaab']    # lazy still expands to reach 'b'
    re.findall(r'(?:xy){1,2}z', 'xyxyz') => ['xyxyz']

Laziness/greediness changes *where the split between adjacent groups falls*, which is the thing a naive engine most often gets subtly wrong:

    re.findall(r'(a+)(a*)', 'aaa')      => [('aaa', '')]
    re.findall(r'(a+?)(a*)', 'aaa')     => [('a', 'aa')]
    re.findall(r'(a*)(a*)(a*)', 'aa')   => [('aa', '', ''), ('', '', '')]
    re.findall(r'(.*)(\d+)', 'a123')    => [('a12', '3')]   # greedy .* gives \d+ one digit
    re.findall(r'(.*?)(\d+)', 'a123')   => [('a', '123')]
    re.findall(r'(a*)(b*)', 'ab')       => [('a', 'b'), ('', '')]
    re.findall(r'a*a', 'aaa')           => ['aaa']
    re.findall(r'a?a?a?aaa', 'aaa')     => ['aaa']
    re.findall(r'a{1,3}ab', 'aaab')     => ['aaab']
    re.findall(r'a.*b.*c', 'abxbxc')    => ['abxbxc']
    re.findall(r'\d+(?:\.\d+)?', '3.')  => ['3']

## C. `$`, `\Z`, `\A`, `^` and MULTILINE

`$` (no MULTILINE) matches at end **and** immediately before a single trailing `\n` — and both positions are real, separate match positions:

    re.findall(r'$', 'ab')       => ['']
    re.findall(r'$', 'ab\n')     => ['', '']        # two matches, at 2 and 3
    re.findall(r'$', 'ab\n\n')   => ['', '']        # only the LAST newline counts; at 3 and 4
    re.findall(r'$', '')         => ['']
    re.findall(r'$', '\n')       => ['', '']
    re.findall(r'$', 'a\r\n')    => ['', '']        # before the \n; \r is not special
    re.sub(r'$', 'X', 'ab\n')    => 'abX\nX'
    re.subn(r'$', 'X', 'ab\n')   => ('abX\nX', 2)
    re.sub(r'$', 'X', 'ab')      => 'abX'
    re.sub(r'$', 'X', '')        => 'X'
    re.split(r'$', 'ab\n')       => ['ab', '\n', '']
    re.findall(r'a$', 'a\n')     => ['a']
    re.findall(r'a$', 'a\nb')    => []
    re.findall(r'a$', 'a\n\n')   => []              # not before a non-final newline
    re.findall(r'.$', 'ab\n')    => ['b']
    re.findall(r'\n$', 'a\n')    => ['\n']          # the \n itself can be the last char matched
    re.findall(r'\d$', '5\n')    => ['5']
    re.sub(r'\.$', '!', 'a.\n')  => 'a!\n'
    re.findall(r'^a*$', 'aa\n')  => ['aa']

`\Z` is Perl's `\z`: absolute end of string, never before the trailing newline. Python has no `\z` at all — it is a hard error, so an engine that silently accepts `\z` (or that implements `\Z` as "end or before final newline") is wrong twice:

    re.findall(r'\Z', 'ab\n')       => ['']         # one match, at 3 only
    re.findall(r'a\Z', 'a\n')       => []           # contrast: r'a$' gives ['a']
    re.sub(r'\Z', 'X', 'ab\n')      => 'ab\nX'      # contrast: r'$' gives 'abX\nX'
    re.findall(r'b\Z', 'ab')        => ['b']
    re.compile(r'\z')               => error: bad escape \z at position 0

`\A` and `\Z` ignore MULTILINE entirely:

    re.findall(r'\Aa', 'a\na', re.M)        => ['a']
    re.findall(r'\Z', 'a\nb', re.M)         => ['']
    re.sub(r'\Z', 'X', 'a\nb\n', flags=re.M)=> 'a\nb\nX'
    re.sub(r'\A', 'X', 'a\nb', flags=re.M)  => 'Xa\nb'

MULTILINE `^` matches at 0 and after every `\n` *including a trailing one*; MULTILINE `$` matches before every `\n` and at end (so a trailing `\n` yields both a position before it and one at end):

    re.findall(r'^', 'a\nb')                 => ['']
    re.findall(r'^', 'a\nb', re.M)           => ['', '']
    re.findall(r'^', 'a\nb\n', re.M)         => ['', '', '']    # 0, 2, 4 — yes, after the final \n
    re.findall(r'^', '\n', re.M)             => ['', '']
    re.findall(r'$', 'a\nb\n', re.M)         => ['', '', '']    # 1, 3, 4
    re.findall(r'$', 'a\n\nb', re.M)         => ['', '', '']
    re.findall(r'^.', 'a\nb\n', re.M)        => ['a', 'b']
    re.findall(r'.$', 'a\nb\n', re.M)        => ['a', 'b']
    re.findall(r'^$', 'a\n\nb', re.M)        => ['']
    re.findall(r'^$', 'a\n\nb\n', re.M)      => ['', '']
    re.sub(r'^', '> ', 'a\nb\n', flags=re.M) => '> a\n> b\n> '  # trailing '> ' surprises people
    re.split(r'^', 'a\nb\n', flags=re.M)     => ['', 'a\n', 'b\n', '']
    re.split(r'$', 'a\nb\n', flags=re.M)     => ['a', '\nb', '\n', '']
    re.sub(r'^|$', 'X', 'a\nb', flags=re.M)  => 'XaX\nXbX'
    re.findall(r'a$|^b', 'a\nb', re.M)       => ['a', 'b']
    re.findall(r'^\s*$', 'a\n \nb', re.M)    => [' ']

Only `\n` is a line terminator — not `\r`, `\v`, `\x85`, `\u2028`:

    re.findall(r'^', 'a\rb', re.M)      => ['']
    re.findall(r'$', 'a\rb', re.M)      => ['']
    re.findall(r'^', 'a\x0bb', re.M)    => ['']
    re.findall(r'^', 'a\x85b', re.M)    => ['']
    re.findall(r'^', 'a\u2028b', re.M)  => ['']
    re.findall(r'\r$', 'a\r\nb', re.M)  => ['\r']       # $ sits before \n, so \r matches
    re.findall(r'^b', 'a\r\nb\r\n', re.M) => ['b']

## D. `.` excludes `\n` only — and only `\n`

    re.findall(r'.', 'a\nb')             => ['a', 'b']
    re.findall(r'.', 'a\nb', re.S)       => ['a', '\n', 'b']
    re.findall(r'a.b', 'a\nb')           => []
    re.findall(r'a.b', 'a\nb', re.S)     => ['a\nb']
    re.findall(r'.*', 'a\nb')            => ['a', '', 'b', '']
    re.findall(r'.*', 'a\nb', re.S)      => ['a\nb', '']
    re.split(r'.', 'a\nb')               => ['', '\n', '']
    re.sub(r'.', 'X', 'a\nb')            => 'X\nX'
    re.findall(r'.', 'a\rb')             => ['a', '\r', 'b']
    re.findall(r'.', 'a\x0bb')           => ['a', '\x0b', 'b']
    re.findall(r'.', 'a\x85b')           => ['a', '\x85', 'b']
    re.findall(r'.', 'a\u2028b')         => ['a', '\u2028', 'b']

Negated classes are *not* affected by DOTALL and never exclude `\n` implicitly:

    re.findall(r'[^x]', 'a\nb')     => ['a', '\n', 'b']
    re.findall(r'[^\n]', 'a\nb')    => ['a', 'b']
    re.findall(r'[\s\S]', 'a\nb')   => ['a', '\n', 'b']

DOTALL × MULTILINE × `$`:

    re.findall(r'.*$', 'ab\n')                => ['ab', '', '']
    re.findall(r'.*$', 'ab\n', re.S)          => ['ab\n', '']
    re.findall(r'^.*$', 'a\nb\n', re.M)       => ['a', 'b', '']
    re.findall(r'^.*$', 'a\nb\n', re.M|re.S)  => ['a\nb\n', '']

## E. `\b` / `\B` at edges

`\b` is `is_word(prev) != is_word(next)`, with out-of-range positions treated as non-word. The empty string therefore has **no** `\b` and also **no** `\B` (a zero-length string has zero positions? no — it has position 0, and Python reports neither, because `\B` in CPython is "not at a boundary AND the string is non-empty at that... " — empirically both are empty):

    re.findall(r'\b', 'ab')        => ['', '']       # positions 0 and 2
    re.findall(r'\b', '')          => []
    re.findall(r'\B', '')          => []             # note: NOT ['']
    re.findall(r'\B', 'ab')        => ['']           # position 1 only
    re.findall(r'\B', 'a')         => []             # 0 and 1 are boundaries; no interior
    re.findall(r'\b', ' ')         => []
    re.findall(r'\B', ' ')         => ['', '']       # positions 0 and 1
    re.findall(r'\b', 'a b')       => ['', '', '', '']
    re.split(r'\b', 'ab cd')       => ['', 'ab', ' ', 'cd', '']
    re.sub(r'\b', '|', 'ab cd')    => '|ab| |cd|'
    re.subn(r'\b', '|', 'ab cd')   => ('|ab| |cd|', 4)
    re.sub(r'\B', '.', 'ab cd')    => 'a.b c.d'
    re.findall(r'\bab\b', 'ab')    => ['ab']
    re.findall(r'\b_\b', '_')      => ['_']          # underscore is a word char
    re.findall(r'\b', '_a')        => ['', '']
    re.findall(r'\b', "don't")     => ['', '', '', '']
    re.findall(r'\b', '3.5')       => ['', '', '', '']
    re.sub(r'\b', '|', '3.5')      => '|3|.|5|'
    re.findall(r'\Bx', 'x ax')     => ['x']
    re.findall(r'\Bab', 'xab ab')  => ['ab']
    re.findall(r'ab\B', 'abx ab')  => ['ab']
    re.findall(r'\bfoo', 'foofoo') => ['foo']
    re.findall(r'foo\b', 'foofoo') => ['foo']
    re.sub(r'\bfoo\b|\bfoobar\b', 'X', 'foobar') => 'X'   # first branch fails \b, second wins

## F. `\w \d \s \b` are Unicode by default (str patterns), and this leaks into `\b`

This is the single largest silent-wrong-answer surface for a from-scratch ASCII engine. If you cannot implement Unicode `\w`/`\d`/`\s` tables in the byte budget, the correct move is to refuse any pattern containing `\w \W \d \D \s \S \b \B` **when the subject string contains a non-ASCII code point** — a value-dependent refusal, not a pattern-dependent one, or you lose the common case.

    re.findall(r'\w+', 'héllo')          => ['héllo']
    re.findall(r'\w', '中')              => ['中']
    re.findall(r'\w+', 'ｆｕｌｌ')          => ['ｆｕｌｌ']       # fullwidth letters
    re.findall(r'\W', 'aéb')             => []
    re.findall(r'\b\w+\b', 'naïve café') => ['naïve', 'café']
    re.findall(r'\b', 'aé')              => ['', '']         # é is a word char: boundaries at 0 and 2
    re.findall(r'\b', '\u0301a')         => ['', '']         # combining acute is NOT \w
    re.findall(r'\w', '\u0301')          => []
    re.findall(r'\w', '½')               => ['½']            # No category: \w yes...
    re.findall(r'\d', '½')               => []               # ...\d no
    re.findall(r'\w', '²')               => ['²']
    re.findall(r'\d', '²')               => []
    re.findall(r'\d', '٣')               => ['٣']            # Arabic-Indic, U+0663
    re.findall(r'\d', '۱')               => ['۱']            # Extended Arabic-Indic, U+06F1
    re.findall(r'\d+', '１２')             => ['１２']          # fullwidth digits
    re.findall(r'\s', 'a\xa0b')          => ['\xa0']         # NBSP IS \s in Python
    re.findall(r'\S', 'a\xa0b')          => ['a', 'b']
    re.findall(r'\s', 'a\x1cb')          => ['\x1c']         # file/group/record separators are \s
    re.findall(r'\s', 'a\x85b')          => ['\x85']
    re.findall(r'\s', 'a\u2028b')        => ['\u2028']
    re.findall(r'\s+', 'a\u200bb')       => []               # ZWSP is NOT \s
    re.split(r'\s+', 'a\xa0b')           => ['a', 'b']
    re.findall(r'\w', '\U0001F600')      => []

## G. Captured span of a quantified group: last iteration wins, and groups are never reset

Python does **not** clear a group's value when a repetition re-enters and takes a different branch. Engines that reset captures per iteration (or that report the first iteration) produce different output.

    re.findall(r'(a)+', 'aaa')            => ['a']            # last 'a', not 'aaa'
    re.findall(r'(ab|cd){2}', 'abcd')     => ['cd']
    re.findall(r'(\w)+', 'abc')           => ['c']
    re.findall(r'(a(b))+', 'abab')        => [('ab', 'b')]
    re.findall(r'(a{2})+', 'aaaa')        => ['aa']
    re.findall(r'(a){2}', 'aa')           => ['a']
    re.findall(r'(a|b)*', 'ab')           => ['b', '']
    re.findall(r'(?:(a)b)*', 'abab')      => ['a', '']
    re.findall(r'(a|ab)*', 'abab')        => ['a', '', 'a', '', '']
    re.findall(r'(a+)+b', 'aaab')         => ['aaa']
    re.findall(r'(?:a(b)?)+', 'aba')      => ['b']            # last rep had no b, but 'b' persists
    re.findall(r'(?:(a)|(b))+', 'ab')     => [('a', 'b')]     # both survive from different reps
    re.findall(r'(?:(a)|(b))+', 'ba')     => [('a', 'b')]     # same tuple, order is group index
    re.findall(r'((a)|(b))+', 'ab')       => [('b', 'a', 'b')]
    re.findall(r'(?:(a)|(b?))+', 'ab')    => [('a', ''), ('', '')]
    re.sub(r'(?:(a)|(b))+', '[\\1|\\2]', 'ab') => '[a|b]'

Groups that never participated:

    re.findall(r'(a)*', 'b')          => ['', '']
    re.findall(r'(a)?b', 'b')         => ['']
    re.findall(r'(a*)*', 'aa')        => ['', '']    # !! outer * ran a second, empty iteration
    re.findall(r'(a*)+', 'b')         => ['', '']
    re.findall(r'(a?)*', 'ab')        => ['', '', '']
    re.findall(r'(a)(b)?', 'ab a')    => [('a', 'b'), ('a', '')]
    re.sub(r'(a)(b)?', '<\\1\\2>', 'ab a') => '<ab> <a>'
    re.sub(r'(a)?b', '[\\1]', 'b')    => '[]'
    re.findall(r'(a)(?:(b)|(c))', 'ab')=> [('a', 'b', '')]

Note `(a*)*` on `'aa'` giving `''`, not `'aa'`: the outer star takes a final zero-width iteration that re-enters the group and captures empty, and *that* is the surviving span. This one catches almost every hand-rolled engine.

## H. Empty matches — the 3.7+ adjacency rule (findall / sub / subn / split)

Python 3.7 changed this: an empty match **is** allowed immediately after a non-empty match; the scanner only advances one position after an *empty* match. Anything implementing the old "skip empty match adjacent to previous match" rule diverges on nearly every `*`-quantified pattern.

    re.findall(r'a*', 'aab')      => ['aa', '', '']
    re.findall(r'x*', 'abxd')     => ['', '', 'x', '', '']
    re.sub(r'x*', '-', 'abxd')    => '-a-b--d-'
    re.subn(r'x*', '-', 'abxd')   => ('-a-b--d-', 5)
    re.sub(r'a*', '-', 'aab')     => '--b-'
    re.subn(r'a*', '-', 'aab')    => ('--b-', 3)
    re.findall(r'b*', 'abc')      => ['', 'b', '', '']
    re.sub(r'b*', '-', 'abc')     => '-a--c-'
    re.findall(r'', 'ab')         => ['', '', '']
    re.sub(r'', '-', 'ab')        => '-a-b-'
    re.findall(r'a*', '')         => ['']
    re.sub(r'a*', '-', '')        => '-'
    re.subn(r'', '-', '')         => ('-', 1)
    re.findall(r'\s*', 'a b')     => ['', ' ', '', '']
    re.findall(r'a{0}', 'aa')     => ['', '', '']
    re.findall(r'(?:ab){0,2}', 'ababab') => ['abab', 'ab', '']
    re.findall(r'a{,3}', 'aaa')   => ['aaa', '']    # a{,3} is {0,3}, not a literal

Anchored empty matches at the end, a classic strip-idiom trap:

    re.findall(r'x*$', 'ax')      => ['x', '']
    re.sub(r'x*$', '-', 'ax')     => 'a--'
    re.sub(r'x*$', '-', 'a')      => 'a-'
    re.findall(r'x*$', 'ax\n')    => ['x', '', '']
    re.findall(r'a*$', 'aa')      => ['aa', '']
    re.sub(r'a*$', 'X', 'aa')     => 'XX'
    re.findall(r'b*$', 'ab\n')    => ['b', '', '']
    re.findall(r'^|$', 'ab')      => ['', '']
    re.findall(r'^|$', 'ab\n')    => ['', '', '']
    re.sub(r'^|$', '#', 'ab')     => '#ab#'
    re.findall(r'\A|\Z', 'ab')    => ['', '']

`re.split` on zero-width matches (allowed since 3.7; used to raise/return the input unsplit):

    re.split(r'x*', 'axbxc')      => ['', 'a', '', 'b', '', 'c', '']
    re.split(r'', 'ab')           => ['', 'a', 'b', '']
    re.split(r'', '')             => ['', '']
    re.split(r'x*', '')           => ['', '']
    re.split(r'\d*', 'a1b2c')     => ['', 'a', '', 'b', '', 'c', '']
    re.split(r'\b', 'ab cd')      => ['', 'ab', ' ', 'cd', '']
    re.split(r'$', 'ab\n')        => ['ab', '\n', '']
    re.split(r',|$', 'a,b')       => ['a', 'b', '']
    re.split(r'\n', 'a\nb\n')     => ['a', 'b', '']

## I. Nested quantifiers, the empty-body repeat rule, and blowup

A repetition whose body matched empty must stop repeating (otherwise you loop forever), but the empty iteration still *happens* and still writes captures — see `(a*)*` in §G.

    re.findall(r'(?:a*)*', 'b')      => ['', '']
    re.findall(r'(?:a*)*', 'aa')     => ['aa', '']
    re.findall(r'(?:a*)+', 'aa')     => ['aa', '']
    re.findall(r'(?:a*)?', 'aa')     => ['aa', '']
    re.findall(r'(?:a*){2,3}', 'aa') => ['aa', '']
    re.findall(r'(?:a*b*)*', 'ab')   => ['ab', '']
    re.findall(r'(?:a?)*b', 'aab')   => ['aab']
    re.findall(r'(?:a+)+b', 'aaab')  => ['aaab']
    re.findall(r'(?:a{2}){2}', 'aaaa')=> ['aaaa']
    re.findall(r'(?:a|b)*c', 'ababX')=> []
    re.findall(r'(?:a*)*b', 'aaac')  => []

Cost, not correctness, but it matters for the exit-90 contract: CPython's own engine is exponential here, so "output-identical" is achievable but a step budget is not optional. Measured on this box: `re.findall(r'(?:a+)+b', 'a'*n + 'c')` → `[]` in 0.004 s (n=16), 0.055 s (n=20), 0.224 s (n=22), 0.918 s (n=24). If your engine hits a step ceiling it must **refuse (exit 90)**, never return "no match" — a budget that silently answers `[]` is exactly the MISMATCH-that-looks-like-success this project forbids.

## J. Return shapes: `''` in findall/sub, `None` in split

Group count decides findall's element type, and a non-participating group is `''` in findall and in a sub template but `None` in split. Three different renderings of the same underlying "group did not match".

    re.findall(r'a', 'aa')          => ['a', 'a']
    re.findall(r'(a)', 'aa')        => ['a', 'a']         # not [('a',), ('a',)]
    re.findall(r'(a)(b)', 'ab')     => [('a', 'b')]
    re.findall(r'(?:a)(b)', 'ab')   => ['b']              # non-capturing doesn't count
    re.findall(r'((a))', 'a')       => [('a', 'a')]
    re.findall(r'(a)|(b)', 'ab')    => [('a', ''), ('', 'b')]
    re.findall(r'(a)|b', 'ab')      => ['a', '']
    re.sub(r'(a)|(b)', '<\\1\\2>', 'ab')      => '<a><b>'   # unmatched group -> '' since 3.5
    re.sub(r'(a)(?:(b)|(c))', '[\\1\\2\\3]', 'ab') => '[ab]'
    re.split(r'(,)', 'a,b')         => ['a', ',', 'b']
    re.split(r'(?:,)', 'a,b')       => ['a', 'b']
    re.split(r'(,)|(;)', 'a,b;c')   => ['a', ',', None, 'b', None, ';', 'c']
    re.split(r'(a)*', 'b')          => ['', None, 'b', None, '']
    re.split(r'(x)*', 'axb')        => ['', None, 'a', 'x', '', None, 'b', None, '']
    re.split(r'(a)(b)?', 'xaby xa') => ['x', 'a', 'b', 'y x', 'a', None, '']

## K. `count` / `maxsplit` sign conventions

Negative is not "unlimited" — it means "do nothing", and the two functions disagree about zero.

    re.sub(r'a', 'X', 'aaa', count=2)   => 'XXa'
    re.sub(r'a', 'X', 'aaa', count=0)   => 'XXX'      # 0 = unlimited
    re.sub(r'a', 'X', 'aaa', count=-1)  => 'aaa'      # negative = no replacements
    re.subn(r'a', 'X', 'aaa', count=-1) => ('aaa', 0)
    re.split(r',', 'a,b,c', maxsplit=0) => ['a', 'b', 'c']   # 0 = unlimited
    re.split(r',', 'a,b,c', maxsplit=1) => ['a', 'b,c']
    re.split(r',', 'a,b,c', maxsplit=-1)=> ['a,b,c']         # negative = no splits
    re.split(r'x*', 'axbxc', maxsplit=2)=> ['', 'a', 'bxc']
    re.split(r'\b', 'a b', maxsplit=2)  => ['', 'a', ' b']

## L. IGNORECASE is Unicode simple-case-folding (if you support `re.I` at all)

    re.findall(r'k', '\u212a', re.I)      => ['\u212a']   # KELVIN SIGN matches 'k'
    re.findall(r'[a-z]', '\u212a', re.I)  => ['\u212a']   # and it's inside the range a-z!
    re.findall(r's', '\u017f', re.I)      => ['\u017f']   # LONG S matches 's'
    re.findall(r'\u03c3', '\u03c2', re.I) => ['\u03c2']   # final sigma == sigma
    re.findall(r'i', '\u0130', re.I)      => ['\u0130']   # dotted capital I matches 'i'
    re.findall(r'\u00e9', '\u00c9', re.I) => ['\u00c9']
    re.findall(r'ss', '\xdf', re.I)       => []           # NO full casefolding for ß
    re.findall(r'[^a]', 'A', re.I)        => []           # negation applies after folding

If you cannot ship the case-folding table, refuse `re.I` outright, or refuse it whenever pattern or subject is non-ASCII. Silent ASCII-only `re.I` gets `[a-z]` vs U+212A wrong in a way no user will ever notice.

## M. `re.escape` must round-trip through your parser

3.7+ escapes only `()[]{}?*+-|^$\.&~#` plus space, `\t\n\r\v\f`. It leaves letters, digits, `_`, and most punctuation alone, and it emits **backslash + literal control character** — so the parser must accept `\` followed by a raw newline/tab as that literal character, and must accept `\ `, `\&`, `\~`, `\#`, `\-`.

    re.escape('a-b')             => 'a\\-b'
    re.escape('a b')             => 'a\\ b'
    re.escape('a#b')             => 'a\\#b'
    re.escape('a&b~c')           => 'a\\&b\\~c'
    re.escape('a/b,c!d"e:f')     => 'a/b,c!d"e:f'      # unchanged
    re.escape('<>@%')            => '<>@%'             # unchanged
    re.escape('a_1')             => 'a_1'
    re.escape('é')               => 'é'
    re.escape('')                => ''
    re.escape('\x00')            => '\x00'             # NUL is NOT escaped
    re.escape('\x07')            => '\x07'
    re.escape('a\nb')            => 'a\\\nb'           # backslash + real newline
    re.escape('a\tb')            => 'a\\\tb'
    len(re.escape('\v\f\r'))     => 6
    re.findall(re.escape('a b'), 'a b')   => ['a b']
    re.findall(re.escape('\n'), 'a\nb')   => ['\n']
    re.findall(re.escape('.'), 'a.b')     => ['.']
    re.sub(re.escape('$'), 'X', 'a$b')    => 'aXb'
    re.findall(re.escape('\x00'), 'a\x00b') => ['\x00']
    re.findall(r'\-', 'a-b')     => ['-']
    re.findall(r'\ ', 'a b')     => [' ']

## N. Positions are code points, not bytes

A Rust engine over `&str` bytes will produce wrong indices, wrong empty-match advance, and split UTF-8 sequences.

    len('\U0001F600')                  => 1
    re.findall(r'.', '\U0001F600')     => ['\U0001f600']
    re.sub(r'.', 'X', 'é\U0001F600')   => 'XX'
    re.findall(r'', '\U0001F600')      => ['', '']     # two positions, not five
    re.sub(r'', '-', '\U0001F600')     => '-\U0001f600-'
    re.findall(r'$', 'a\U0001F600')    => ['']

## O. Things that must be an error or a refusal, never a silent guess

    re.compile(r'\z')       => error: bad escape \z at position 0
    re.compile(r'\Q')       => error: bad escape \Q at position 0
    re.compile(r'[]')       => error: unterminated character set at position 0
    re.compile(r'[^]')      => error: unterminated character set at position 0
    re.compile(r'a{2,1}')   => error: min repeat greater than max repeat at position 2
    re.compile(r'*a')       => error: nothing to repeat at position 0
    re.compile(r'a**')      => error: multiple repeat at position 2
    re.compile(r'a{1}{2}')  => error: multiple repeat at position 4
    re.compile(r'[a-\d]')   => error: bad character range a-\d at position 1
    re.sub(r'(a)|(b)', '\\3', 'ab') => error: invalid group reference 3 at position 1
    re.sub(r'a', '\\q', 'a')        => error: bad escape \q at position 0

But these are *valid* and must not be refused as syntax errors (they are ordinary literals / accepted forms):

    re.compile(r'a{,3}')          => compiles; equals a{0,3}
    re.findall(r'a{,3}', 'aaa')   => ['aaa', '']
    re.findall(r'a{2', 'a{2')     => ['a{2']       # unclosed brace is a literal
    re.findall(r'a{}', 'a{}')     => ['a{}']
    re.findall(r'[]a]', 'a')      => ['a']         # ']' first in a class is literal
    re.findall(r'[a-]', 'a-')     => ['a', '-']
    re.findall(r'[\-a]', '-a')    => ['-', 'a']
    re.findall(r'[a^]', '^')      => ['^']
    re.findall(r'[$.|*+()]', 'a.b')=> ['.']
    re.findall(r'[\b]', 'a\bb')   => ['\x08']      # \b inside a class is BACKSPACE, not a boundary
    re.findall(r'\0', 'a\x00b')   => ['\x00']
    re.findall(r'\x41', 'A')      => ['A']
    re.findall(r'\101', 'A')      => ['A']         # octal escape
    re.findall(r'\N{BULLET}', '•')=> ['\u2022']    # named Unicode escape, in scope for str patterns
    re.findall(r'[\x41-\x43]', 'ABCD') => ['A', 'B', 'C']
    re.sub(r'a', '\\n', 'a')      => '\n'          # template escapes are interpreted

Two more that your subset says are refused but that Python accepts, so the refusal must fire at parse time and not be mistaken for a literal: `re.compile(r'(?i)a')` compiles to `re.compile('(?i)a', re.IGNORECASE)`, `re.split(r'(?=x)', 'axb')` → `['a', 'xb']`, `re.sub(r'(?m)^', '> ', 'a\nb')` → `'> a\n> b'`, `re.findall(r'(a*)b\1', 'aabaa')` → `['aa']`. And `re.split(r'(?:)', 'ab')` → `['', 'a', 'b', '']` — an empty non-capturing group is legal.

## Highest-value picks if you can only afford a small differential suite

`re.sub(r'x*', '-', 'abxd')` → `'-a-b--d-'`; `re.sub(r'$', 'X', 'ab\n')` → `'abX\nX'`; `re.sub(r'\Z', 'X', 'ab\n')` → `'ab\nX'`; `re.sub(r'^', '> ', 'a\nb\n', flags=re.M)` → `'> a\n> b\n> '`; `re.findall(r'(a*)*', 'aa')` → `['', '']`; `re.findall(r'(?:(a)|(b))+', 'ab')` → `[('a','b')]`; `re.split(r'(x)*', 'axb')` → `['', None, 'a', 'x', '', None, 'b', None, '']`; `re.findall(r'a|ab', 'ab')` → `['a']`; `re.findall(r'\B', '')` → `[]`; `re.findall(r'\d', '٣')` → `['٣']`; `re.sub(r'x*$', '-', 'ax')` → `'a--'`; `re.escape('a\nb')` → `'a\\\nb'`.

---

All pairs below were run and verified on this box against `Python 3.11.15 (main, Mar 3 2026)` — probe scripts left in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-lypning/13f3494a-8f12-5202-84b8-45addf9cef2c/scratchpad/p1.py` … `p9.py` if you want to re-run them.

# 0. The one algorithm that generates half of these bugs: MUST_ADVANCE

`findall`, `finditer`, `sub`, `subn` and `split` all share one scan loop, and since 3.7 it is **not** "on an empty match, bump pos by 1". It is:

```
pos = 0; must_advance = False
while pos <= len(s):
    m = search(s, pos, must_advance)   # a match STARTING AT pos is rejected if it is zero-width
    if m is None: break
    <consume m>
    must_advance = (m.end() == m.start())
    pos = m.end()
```

The subtlety a naive port gets wrong: `must_advance` forbids a **zero-width match at the starting position only**. A zero-width match found *later* in the same `search` is accepted, and a *non-empty* match starting at that same position is also accepted. So an empty match is immediately followed by a retry at the *same* index that can still succeed.

Consequences, all counter-intuitive:

- `re.findall(r'a*?', 'aa')` → `['', 'a', '', 'a', '']` — five results for a two-character string. (`''`@0, then `'a'`@0-1 from the retry at 0, then `''`@1, `'a'`@1-2, `''`@2.)
- `re.findall(r'a??', 'aa')` → `['', 'a', '', 'a', '']` (identical).
- `re.findall(r'b*', 'abbbc')` → `['', 'bbb', '', '']` — note the `'bbb'` is found by the *must_advance retry* that started scanning at 0 and slid to 1.
- `re.findall(r'a*', 'aab')` → `['aa', '', '']`
- `re.findall(r'x*', 'abc')` → `['', '', '', '']` (len+1 results)
- `re.findall(r'', 'abc')` → `['', '', '', '']`
- `re.findall(r'(?:)', '')` → `['']`; `re.findall(r'a*', '')` → `['']`; `re.findall(r'a+', '')` → `[]`
- `re.findall(r'a|', 'aba')` → `['a', '', 'a', '']`
- `re.sub(r'a*', 'X', 'baac')` → `'XbXXcX'` (six replacements, four input chars)
- `re.sub(r'a*?', '-', 'aa')` → `'-----'`
- `re.sub(r'b*', '-', 'abbbc')` → `'-a--c-'`

A "bump by one after empty match" implementation gives `['', 'bbb', '']` for the third case and `'-a-c-'` for the last — wrong, silently.

Zero-width assertions ride the same loop:
- `re.findall(r'\b', 'ab cd')` → `['', '', '', '']`; `re.findall(r'\B', 'ab cd')` → `['', '']`
- `re.findall(r'^', 'abc')` → `['']` (no MULTILINE); `re.findall(r'^a', 'a\na')` → `['a']`
- `re.findall(r'$', 'abc')` → `['']` but `re.findall(r'$', 'abc\n')` → `['', '']` (`$` matches before a final newline **and** at end)
- `re.findall(r'\Z', 'ab\n')` → `['']` (only one — `\Z` is true end only)
- `re.sub(r'$', '<', 'ab\n')` → `'ab<\n<'` — a great differential case; `re.sub(r'\Z', '!', 'ab\n')` → `'ab\n!'`
- `re.sub(r'\b', '|', 'ab cd')` → `'|ab| |cd|'`
- `re.sub(r'^', '>', 'ab')` → `'>ab'`
- `re.findall(r'.$', 'ab\ncd')` → `['d']` (`.` doesn't match `\n`, `$` before-final-newline doesn't apply here)

# 1. findall: the return-shape rule is arity-driven, not value-driven

The rule is the count of **capturing** groups in the compiled pattern (`(?:...)` doesn't count), decided once, not per match:

- 0 groups → list of whole-match strings: `re.findall(r'a.', 'abac')` → `['ab', 'ac']`; `re.findall(r'(?:ab)', 'abab')` → `['ab', 'ab']`
- exactly 1 group → list of that group's string, **not** the whole match: `re.findall(r'a(?:b)(c)', 'abc')` → `['c']` (not `['abc']`); `re.findall(r'(a)', 'aaa')` → `['a','a','a']`
- 2+ groups → list of **tuples**: `re.findall(r'(a)(b)', 'abab')` → `[('a','b'), ('a','b')]`

Non-participating groups become `''` in findall (they become `None` in split — see §5, this asymmetry is a classic):
- `re.findall(r'(a)(b)?', 'ab a')` → `[('a', 'b'), ('a', '')]`
- `re.findall(r'(a)(b)(c)?', 'abcab')` → `[('a','b','c'), ('a','b','')]`
- `re.findall(r'(a)|(b)', 'ab')` → `[('a', ''), ('', 'b')]`
- `re.findall(r'(a*)b', 'b')` → `['']` — group participated and matched empty; indistinguishable from non-participation in findall's output, but not in split's.

Group numbering is by opening-paren order, outer first:
- `re.findall(r'((a)(b))', 'ab')` → `[('ab', 'a', 'b')]`
- `re.findall(r'(a(b)?)', 'a')` → `[('a', '')]`

A quantified group keeps its **last successful** repetition, and keeps a value from an earlier iteration even when the last iteration went down the other branch:
- `re.findall(r'(a)*', 'aa')` → `['a', '']` (two results: `'aa'`@0-2 with group=`'a'`, then the empty match at 2 where the group never participated)
- `re.findall(r'(a)*', 'b')` → `['', '']`
- `re.findall(r'(?:(a)|(b))+', 'ab')` → `[('a', 'b')]` — group 1 still holds `'a'` from the first iteration.

Counted quantifiers:
- `re.findall(r'a{0}', 'aa')` → `['', '', '']`
- `re.findall(r'a{0,}', 'aa')` → `['aa', '']`
- `re.findall(r'a{2,3}?', 'aaaa')` → `['aa', 'aa']`

Signature trap: `re.findall(pattern, string, flags=0)` — the third positional is **flags**, not a count. `re.findall(r'a', 'aA', re.I)` → `['a', 'A']`.

# 2. sub/subn: the replacement template

The template is parsed **eagerly**, before any scanning, and a bad template raises even when the pattern never matches:
- `re.sub(r'zzz', r'\1', 'abc')` → raises `re.error: invalid group reference 1 at position 1` (does **not** return `'abc'`)
- `re.sub(r'zzz', r'\q', 'abc')` → raises `re.error: bad escape \q at position 0`
- `re.subn(r'zzz', r'\9', 'abc')` → same eager raise
- But a *function* repl is never called when there is no match: `re.sub(r'zzz', lambda m: 1/0, 'abc')` → `'abc'`

Group references:
- `re.sub(r'(a)(b)', r'\2\1', 'ab')` → `'ba'`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\g<1>\g<1>', 'a')` → `'aa'`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\g<0>!', 'a')` → `'a!'` (group 0 = whole match); `re.sub(r'x*', r'[\g<0>]', 'ab')` → `'[]a[]b[]'`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\g<01>', 'a')` → `'a'` (leading zeros in `\g<>` are fine)
- Unmatched group substitutes as **empty string**, not an error (this changed in 3.5): `re.sub(r'(a)(b)?', r'[\2]', 'a')` → `'[]'`; `re.sub(r'(x)?a', r'[\1]', 'a')` → `'[]'`; `re.sub(r'(a)|(b)', r'[\1\2]', 'ab')` → `'[a][b]'`
- Quantified group: `re.sub(r'(\w)+', r'<\1>', 'abc')` → `'<c>'`; `re.sub(r'(a)*', r'[\1]', 'xaay')` → `'[]x[a][]y[]'`

Escapes recognised in the template (note: **not** the same set as in a pattern):
- `re.sub(r'a', r'\\', 'a')` → `'\\'` (one backslash)
- `re.sub(r'a', r'\n', 'a')` → newline; `r'\t\r\f\v\a\b'` → `'\t\r\x0c\x0b\x07\x08'` — **`\b` in a template is backspace `\x08`**, not a word boundary
- Octal: `re.sub(r'a', r'\0', 'a')` → `'\x00'`; `r'\00'` → `'\x00'`; `r'\000'` → `'\x00'`; `r'\0000'` → `'\x000'` (three octal digits max after `\0`); `r'\101'` → `'A'`; `r'\1010'` → `'A0'`; `r'\377'` → `'ÿ'`
- **Not** recognised, all raise: `re.sub(r'a', r'\x41', 'a')` → `re.error: bad escape \x at position 0`; `r'\N{BULLET}'` → `bad escape \N`; `r'\d'` → `bad escape \d`; `r'\s'` → `bad escape \s`; `re.sub(r'(a)', '\\', 'a')` → `re.error: bad escape (end of pattern) at position 0`
- No `$&`/`&` semantics at all: `re.sub(r'a', 'x$&y', 'a')` → `'x$&y'`; `re.sub(r'a', '&', 'a')` → `'&'`

The digits-after-backslash disambiguation is the fiddly bit. Exact rule from `sre_parse.parse_template`: if the first digit is `0`, it is octal (up to 3 digits total). Otherwise read a second digit if present; it is octal **only if** all three of first-digit, second-digit and the *next* character are octal digits (i.e. a full 3-digit octal run); otherwise it is a group number of however many digits were read (max 2):
- `re.sub(r'(1)(2)(3)(4)(5)(6)(7)(8)(9)(a)(b)(c)', r'[\12]', '123456789abc')` → `'[c]'` (group 12)
- same pattern with `r'[\11]'` → `'[b]'`, `r'[\10]'` → `'[a]'`, `r'[\012]'` → `'[\n]'` (octal, leading zero), `r'[\g<12>]'` → `'[c]'`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\10', 'a')` → `re.error: invalid group reference 10 at position 1` (**not** group 1 followed by `'0'`) — whereas `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\g<1>0', 'a')` → `'a0'`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\77', 'a')` → `invalid group reference 77` (two digits → group ref)
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\777', 'a')` → `re.error: octal escape value \777 outside of range 0-0o377 at position 0`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\400', 'a')` → `octal escape value \400 outside of range 0-0o377`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\378', 'a')` → `invalid group reference 37` (the `8` is not an octal digit, so `\37` is a group ref, not `\37`+`'8'`)
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\19', 'a')` → `invalid group reference 19`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\08', 'a')` → `'\x008'`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\1a', 'a')` → `'aa'`
- `re.sub(r'a', r'\8', 'a')` → `invalid group reference 8 at position 1`

Malformed `\g<...>` — note the *different exception types*:
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\g<2>', 'a')` → `re.error: invalid group reference 2 at position 3`
- `re.sub(r'a', r'\g<A>', 'a')` → **`IndexError: unknown group name 'A'`** (not `re.error`)
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\g<>', 'a')` → `re.error: missing group name at position 3`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\g<1', 'a')` → `re.error: missing >, unterminated name at position 3`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\g1', 'a')` → `re.error: missing < at position 2`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\g<-1>', 'a')` → `re.error: bad character in group name '-1' at position 3`
- `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\g< 1 >', 'a')` → returns `'a'` **and writes a `DeprecationWarning: bad character in group name ' 1 ' at position 3` to stderr**. Byte-identical stdout is not enough here; this one should simply be refused.

Function repl: fully supported by CPython, receives a `Match`, must return `str` (or `bytes` for bytes patterns):
- `re.sub(r'\d+', lambda m: str(int(m.group())*2), 'a3b10')` → `'a6b20'`
- The return value is **not** template-expanded: `re.sub(r'a', lambda m: r'\1', 'a')` → `'\\1'`
- `re.sub(r'a', lambda m: 1, 'a')` → `TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, int found`
- Since Match is deferred in this step, **a callable repl must be a refusal**, not a "close enough" path.

Type mixing: `re.sub(r'a', b'-', 'abc')` → `TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, bytes found`. Bytes patterns work end-to-end: `re.findall(rb'a.', b'abac')` → `[b'ab', b'ac']`, `re.sub(rb'a', b'-', b'abc')` → `b'-bc'`.

# 3. sub/subn: count, and empty-match substitution

`re.sub(pattern, repl, string, count=0, flags=0)` — the 4th positional is count, the 5th is flags:
- `re.sub(r'a', '-', 'aaaa', 2)` → `'--aa'` (positional count is fine in 3.11; it only became a DeprecationWarning in 3.13)
- `count=0` means **unlimited**: `re.sub(r'a', '-', 'aaaa', 0)` → `'----'`
- **Negative count means zero replacements**, not unlimited: `re.sub(r'a', '-', 'aaaa', -1)` → `'aaaa'`
- `re.sub(r'a', '-', 'aaaa', 99)` → `'----'`
- `re.sub(r'a', '-', 'aaa', None)` → `TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`
- `re.sub(r'a', '-', 'aaa', True)` → `'-aa'` (bools are ints)
- Count applies to matches including empty ones: `re.sub(r'', '-', 'abc', 2)` → `'-a-bc'`
- `re.sub(r'a', '-', 'A', 0, re.I)` → `'-'`; `re.sub(re.compile('a'), '-', 'a', 0, re.I)` → `ValueError: cannot process flags argument with a compiled pattern`

Empty-match substitution (same MUST_ADVANCE loop; the un-matched text between matches is copied verbatim):
- `re.sub(r'', '-', 'abc')` → `'-a-b-c-'`
- `re.sub(r'x*', '-', 'abc')` → `'-a-b-c-'`
- `re.sub(r'', '-', '')` → `'-'`; `re.sub(r'x*', '-', '')` → `'-'`
- `re.sub(r'a*', '-', 'aab')` → `'--b-'`
- `re.sub(r'a|', '-', 'aba')` → `'--b--'`

`subn` returns `(new_string, number_of_subs_performed)`, where the count counts matches (including empty and including no-op replacements), not changed characters:
- `re.subn(r'a', '-', 'aaaa', 2)` → `('--aa', 2)`
- `re.subn(r'x', '-', 'abc')` → `('abc', 0)`
- `re.subn(r'', '-', 'ab')` → `('-a-b-', 3)`
- `re.subn(r'a*', '-', 'aab')` → `('--b-', 3)`
- `re.subn(r'x*', '-', 'abc', 2)` → `('-a-bc', 2)`
- `re.subn(r'a*?', '-', 'aa', 3)` → `('---a', 3)`

# 4. split: capturing groups leak into the output

`re.split(pattern, string, maxsplit=0, flags=0)`. Basics:
- `re.split(r',', 'a,b,c')` → `['a','b','c']`
- `re.split(r',', ',a,')` → `['', 'a', '']`
- `re.split(r',', '')` → `['']`
- `re.split(r'x', 'abc')` → `['abc']` (a 1-element list, never `[]`)
- `re.split(r'c', 'abc')` → `['ab', '']`
- `re.split(r'a', 'aaa')` → `['', '', '', '']`
- `re.split(r'\s+', ' a b ')` → `['', 'a', 'b', '']`
- `maxsplit=0` is unlimited; **negative maxsplit returns the whole string unsplit**: `re.split(r',', 'a,b,c', -1)` → `['a,b,c']`; `re.split(r',', 'a,b,c', 1)` → `['a', 'b,c']`; `re.split(r'x', 'abc', 5)` → `['abc']`
- `re.split(r',', 'a,b', None)` → `TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`

Every capturing group in the pattern is **interleaved into the result** after each separator, and a non-participating group contributes **`None`** (contrast findall's `''`):
- `re.split(r'(,)', 'a,b')` → `['a', ',', 'b']`
- `re.split(r'(,)(;)', 'a,;b')` → `['a', ',', ';', 'b']`
- `re.split(r'([,;])|( )', 'a,b c')` → `['a', ',', None, 'b', None, ' ', 'c']`
- `re.split(r'a(b)?', 'xay')` → `['x', None, 'y']`
- `re.split(r'(a)(b)?', 'xaby')` → `['x', 'a', 'b', 'y']`
- `re.split(r'((a)(b))', 'xaby')` → `['x', 'ab', 'a', 'b', 'y']`
- A group that participated and matched empty gives `''`, not `None`: `re.split(r'(a*)b', 'b')` → `['', '', '']`
- `re.split(r'(\d)+', 'a123b')` → `['a', '3', 'b']` (last repetition only)
- `re.split(r'(?:,)', 'a,b')` → `['a', 'b']` (non-capturing contributes nothing)
- Groups are emitted for each split, and maxsplit counts splits not list items: `re.split(r'(,)', 'a,b,c', 1)` → `['a', ',', 'b,c']`; `re.split(r'(,)|(;)', 'a,b;c', 1)` → `['a', ',', None, 'b;c']`

Empty-match splitting (3.7+; in 3.5/3.6 these raised `ValueError`, and pre-3.5 they silently didn't split — so any implementation modelled on old docs is wrong):
- `re.split(r'', 'abc')` → `['', 'a', 'b', 'c', '']`
- `re.split(r'x*', 'abc')` → `['', 'a', 'b', 'c', '']`
- `re.split(r'', '')` → `['', '']` (two elements!)
- `re.split(r'', 'abc', 2)` → `['', 'a', 'bc']`
- `re.split(r'\b', 'ab cd')` → `['', 'ab', ' ', 'cd', '']`
- `re.split(r'\s*', 'a b')` → `['', 'a', '', 'b', '']`
- `re.split(r'a*', 'abc')` → `['', '', 'b', 'c', '']` — note the double `''` at the front
- `re.split(r'b*', 'abbbc')` → `['', 'a', '', 'c', '']`
- `re.split(r'^', 'ab\ncd')` → `['', 'ab\ncd']` (no MULTILINE)
- `re.split(r'(?:)', 'ab', 1)` → `['', 'ab']`
- Empty pattern *with* a group: `re.split(r'()', 'ab')` → `['', '', 'a', '', 'b', '', '']` and `re.split(r'()', 'ab', 1)` → `['', '', 'ab']`
- The nastiest single case I found, worth putting in verbatim: `re.split(r'(a)*', 'xaay')` → `['', None, 'x', 'a', '', None, 'y', None, '']`

# 5. re.escape in 3.11

Since 3.7 it escapes exactly the ASCII characters that are special in a regex, plus whitespace and `#` (so the result is also safe under `re.VERBOSE`). The implementation is a translate table built from the literal set `()[]{}?*+-|^$\.&~# \t\n\r\v\f` — **24 characters, and nothing else in ASCII, and nothing at all outside ASCII**. I enumerated all of `chr(0..127)`; the escaped set is exactly:

```
\t \n \x0b \x0c \r  (space) # $ & ( ) * + - . ? [ \ ] ^ { | } ~
```

Notably **not** escaped (3.6 and earlier escaped all non-alphanumerics, so a memory-based implementation will over-escape): `!` `"` `%` `'` `,` `/` `:` `;` `<` `=` `>` `?`→(is escaped) `@` `_` `` ` `` and, crucially, **NUL**: `re.escape('\x00')` → `'\x00'` (3.6 gave `'\\000'`).

Pairs:
- `re.escape('a.b')` → `'a\\.b'`
- `re.escape('1+1=2')` → `'1\\+1=2'` (the `=` is untouched)
- `re.escape('hello world')` → `'hello\\ world'` (the space **is** escaped)
- `re.escape('a-b')` → `'a\\-b'`
- `re.escape('a_b')` → `'a_b'`
- `re.escape('#comment')` → `'\\#comment'`
- `re.escape('a\nb')` → `'a\\\nb'` — a backslash followed by a **literal newline**, not `\\n`
- `re.escape('a\tb')` → `'a\\\tb'`
- `re.escape('C:\\path\\x')` → `'C:\\\\path\\\\x'`
- `re.escape('~user')` → `'\\~user'`
- `re.escape('!@#$%^&*()')` → `'!@\\#\\$%\\^\\&\\*\\(\\)'` (`!`, `@`, `%` untouched)
- `re.escape('a,b')` → `'a,b'`; `re.escape('a/b')` → `'a/b'`; `re.escape('a:b')` → `'a:b'`; `re.escape('a;b')` → `'a;b'`; `re.escape("a'b")` → `"a'b"`; `re.escape('a"b')` → `'a"b'`; `re.escape('a<b>')` → `'a<b>'`; `re.escape('a=b')` → `'a=b'`; `re.escape('`x`')` → `'`x`'`
- `re.escape('')` → `''`
- Non-ASCII untouched: `re.escape('\xa0')` → `'\xa0'`, `re.escape('é')` → `'é'`, `re.escape('\u3000')` → `'\u3000'` (ideographic space — escaped by 3.6, not by 3.7+)
- bytes: `re.escape(b'a.b !')` → `b'a\\.b\\ !'`; `re.escape(b'\x00')` → `b'\x00'`
- `re.escape(5)` → `TypeError: decoding to str: need a bytes-like object, int found`

Round-trip cases worth including because they combine escape with the other four: `re.sub(re.escape('a.b'), 'X', 'a.b axb')` → `'X axb'`, and `re.split(re.escape('.'), 'a.b')` → `['a', 'b']`.

# 6. Things I'd make explicit refusals rather than try to match

- **Callable `repl`** for `sub`/`subn` — it needs a real Match object, which is deferred.
- **`\g< 1 >` and any `\g<name>` with a non-identifier, non-integer name** — CPython emits a `DeprecationWarning` on stderr *and* returns a value; byte-identical means reproducing that warning line, including the filename and line number, which is not worth it.
- **Any path that raises** (`re.error`, `IndexError`, `TypeError`) — CPython exits 1 with a traceback whose text includes `re/_parser.py` frames and line numbers. Reproducing those bytes from Rust is not realistic; refusing (exit 90) hands the program to CPython, which produces them for free. That covers every "RAISES" row above.
- Flags positional-arg confusion: implement the real signatures (`findall(p, s, flags=0)`, `split(p, s, maxsplit=0, flags=0)`, `sub/subn(p, repl, s, count=0, flags=0)`) or refuse when a 3rd/4th/5th positional is present.
- Bytes patterns/strings, if the engine is str-only — refuse rather than approximate; `\w`/`\b` semantics differ between them.

The highest-value differential set, if you only take twenty: `re.findall(r'a*?', 'aa')`, `re.findall(r'b*', 'abbbc')`, `re.findall(r'(a)(b)?', 'ab a')`, `re.findall(r'a(?:b)(c)', 'abc')`, `re.findall(r'$', 'abc\n')`, `re.sub(r'a*', 'X', 'baac')`, `re.sub(r'$', '<', 'ab\n')`, `re.sub(r'a', '-', 'aaaa', -1)`, `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\10', 'a')`, `re.sub(r'…12 groups…', r'[\12]', …)`, `re.sub(r'(a)', r'\012', 'a')`, `re.sub(r'a', r'\b', 'a')`, `re.sub(r'zzz', r'\1', 'abc')`, `re.subn(r'', '-', 'ab')`, `re.split(r'(a)*', 'xaay')`, `re.split(r'([,;])|( )', 'a,b c')`, `re.split(r'a*', 'abc')`, `re.split(r'', '')`, `re.split(r',', 'a,b,c', -1)`, `re.escape('a\nb')`.

---

Verified everything below against the local CPython — `Python 3.11.15 (main, Mar 3 2026)` — today, 2026-08-31. Every pair is a copy of real output, not recall. Timings are from this machine.

---

# 0. The rule that governs all the others: refusal must happen before the program has done anything

This is the finding that reorders the rest of the list. Exit 90 means "nothing happened, CPython will run this from scratch." A refusal is only sound while that is still true. A regex refusal discovered at *match* time — after the program has printed three lines, appended to a log, or written a file — is not a refusal, it is a double execution. Invariant 2's "a dispatcher that retried on exit 1 would run a half-completed program twice" applies verbatim to a late regex refusal, and stdout emptiness is not sufficient evidence of innocence: `open('out.txt','a').write(...)` leaves stdout clean.

So the decision procedure must be: **scan every `re.*` call site at program-load time, refuse the whole program before executing statement one.** Concretely, at load time:

- a call to `re.findall/sub/subn/split` whose pattern argument is not a string/bytes literal (or a name bound once to one) → refuse the program. You cannot know at load time whether `re.sub(user_pat, ...)` uses a lookbehind.
- a literal pattern outside the subset → refuse the program, not the call.
- any construct whose behaviour depends on the *subject* (§2) → refuse the program, because the subject is runtime data.

Only if you buffer all of stdout and forbid every other side effect (file writes, `os.*`, sockets) until clean exit may you defer a refusal to match time, and even then the step-budget refusal in §6 has to unwind a `re.sub` that has already built half a result string. Static, load-time refusal is much cheaper than either, and over-refusal is free by invariant 1.

---

# 1. Flags

Refuse any call whose `flags` argument is present and not statically `0` / absent, and refuse any pattern containing an inline flag group. Two of these are worse than merely unsupported:

**`re.DEBUG` writes the parse tree to stdout.** `python3 -c "import re; re.findall('a(b)','ab',re.DEBUG)"` puts on **stdout**:

```
LITERAL 97
SUBPATTERN 1 0 0
  LITERAL 98

 0. INFO 10 0b1 2 2 (to 11)
      prefix_skip 1
      prefix [0x61, 0x62] ('ab')
      overlap [0, 0]
11: LITERAL 0x61 ('a')
13. MARK 0
15. LITERAL 0x62 ('b')
17. MARK 1
19. SUCCESS
```

stderr empty. If the engine silently ignored DEBUG it would produce a program whose entire stdout is missing. Refuse.

**`re.LOCALE` on a str pattern raises, and the message is the output.** `re.findall('a','A',re.LOCALE)` → `ValueError: cannot use LOCALE flag with a str pattern`. With a bytes pattern it is legal and depends on the process locale: `re.findall(b'a', b'A', re.LOCALE)` → `[]` here, but not necessarily elsewhere. Refuse both; the second can never be byte-identical by construction.

The rest, with the pairs that show they are not cosmetic:

- `re.I` — see §2, it is a Unicode problem, not a case problem.
- `re.M` — `re.findall('^b','a\nb')` → `[]` but `re.findall('^b','a\nb',re.M)` → `['b']`.
- `re.S` — `re.findall('a.b','a\nb')` → `[]`, with `re.S` → `['a\nb']`.
- `re.X` — reparses the whole pattern; `re.findall('a b','ab',re.X)` → `['ab']`.
- `re.A` — the *only* flag that makes your life easier (it collapses §2 entirely). `re.findall(r'\w+','café',re.A)` → `['caf']`. Consider supporting exactly this one rather than refusing it; it is the flag under which a byte-oriented engine is trivially correct.
- `re.U` — a no-op on str patterns; `re.findall('a','a',re.U)` → `['a']`. Safe to accept as equivalent to no flags. Refusing it is also fine.
- **flags passed as a bare int**: `re.findall('a','A',2)` → `['A']`. `2 == re.I`. A check for `flags is re.I` misses this; check the integer value.
- **flags passed positionally to `sub`/`subn`/`split`**: in 3.11 `re.sub(pat, repl, s, count, flags)` — 5 positional args are legal. `re.sub('a','x','abc',1,re.I)` is valid here (it is only deprecated from 3.13). Do not assume `flags` is keyword-only.
- **inline flags all parse in 3.11 and must be refused, not errored**: `re.sub('(?i)a','X','A')` → `'X'`; `re.findall('(?i:a)','A')` → `['A']`; `re.findall('(?-i:a)','a')` → `['a']`; `re.findall('(?a)','aaa')` → `['','','','']`; `re.findall('(?s).','a\nb')` → `['a','\n','b']`. But **`re.findall('a(?i)b','AB')` → `re.error: global flags not at the start of the expression at position 1`** — a mid-pattern global flag is an error, an anchored one is not. Do not conflate.
- **flags with a compiled pattern**: `re.findall(re.compile('a',re.I),'aA',re.I)` → `ValueError: cannot process flags argument with a compiled pattern`. And `re.findall(re.compile('a'),'aa')` → `['a','a']` is perfectly legal — a `Pattern` object may be passed to these functions even though `compile` is deferred. Refuse any call whose first argument is not a literal.

---

# 2. Unicode: the constructs whose meaning is a property of the *subject*, not the pattern

Under the default (Unicode) mode, `\w \d \s \W \D \S \b \B` and case-folding are all defined by Unicode tables. Shipping those tables costs far more than 16 KB. The refusal line therefore has to be: **any pattern using `\w \d \s \W \D \S \b \B`, or any case-insensitive matching, is refused unless the engine can prove both pattern and subject are pure ASCII — and since the subject is runtime data, that proof does not exist at load time.** So: refuse the program at load time if a literal pattern contains any of those escapes, unless you also implement the ASCII-only fast path *and* gate it on a runtime check that must happen before any output (§0).

The pairs that show the tables are not small:

**`\d` is Nd, not `[0-9]`.**
- `re.findall(r'\d+','٣٤')` → `['٣٤']` (Arabic-Indic digits)
- `re.findall(r'\d+','１２')` → `['１２']` (fullwidth)
- `re.findall(r'\d','٠Ⅰ²፩')` → `['٠']` — Roman numeral Ⅰ, superscript ², Ethiopic ፩ are **not** `\d`

**`\w` is Unicode alphanumeric plus `_`, and it is wider than "letters".**
- `re.findall(r'\w+','naïve café')` → `['naïve','café']`
- `re.findall(r'\w+','日本語abc')` → `['日本語abc']`
- `re.findall(r'\w','ª²½')` → `['ª','²','½']` — the ordinal indicator, superscript two and the vulgar fraction all match `\w`, though only one of them is a letter and none is `\d`
- `re.findall(r'\w','_µ́٠Ⅰ〇')` → `['_','µ','٠','Ⅰ','〇']` — note the combining acute U+0301 is **absent**
- `re.sub(r'\W','_','a-é!b')` → `'a_é_b'`

**`\s` is the one nobody guesses right.** In Unicode mode it includes the four C0 separators:
```
re.findall(r'\s', '\x1c\x1d\x1e\x1f\x85\xa0 \t')
  → ['\x1c','\x1d','\x1e','\x1f','\x85','\xa0',' ','\t']
```
and the full set observed is `' \t\n\r\x0b\x0c\x1c\x1d\x1e\x1f\x85\xa0\u1680\u2000..\u200a\u2028\u2029\u202f\u205f\u3000'`. U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE is **not** whitespace. Under ASCII/bytes mode the same string gives only `[' ','\t']`:
```
re.findall(rb'\s', b'\x1c\x1d\x1e\x1f\x85\xa0 \t')  → [b' ', b'\t']
re.findall(r'\s', '\x1c\x1d\x1e\x1f\x85\xa0 \t', re.A) → [' ', '\t']
```
So `\s` differs between the two modes on `\x1c`–`\x1f` and `\x85` — a difference an implementer testing with spaces and tabs will never see.

**`\b` inherits all of it.** `re.findall(r'\b\w+\b','aé')` → `['aé']`, but with `re.A` → `['a']`, and `re.findall(r'\b','aé',re.A)` → `['','']` (two boundaries, because é is a non-word char in ASCII mode).

**`re.I` is Unicode case folding, and simple folding at that.**
- `re.findall('k','\u212a',re.I)` → `['K']` — KELVIN SIGN matches `k`
- `re.findall('[a-z]','\u212a\u017f',re.I)` → `['K','ſ']` — KELVIN and LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S both match the ASCII range `[a-z]`
- `re.findall('ı','I',re.I)` → `['I']` and `re.findall('i','İ',re.I)` → `['İ']` (dotless/dotted I both fold to ASCII, no Turkish special-casing)
- `re.findall('σ','Σς',re.I)` → `['Σ','ς']` (final sigma folds)
- but `re.findall('ss','ß',re.I)` → `[]` and `re.findall('ß','SS',re.I)` → `[]` (no full folding)

An ASCII-only `tolower` gets `[a-z]` vs KELVIN wrong in the direction that silently *misses* a match. Refuse `re.I`.

**Indexing must be by code point, not byte and not UTF-16 unit.** If the Rust side slices a `&str` by byte offsets anywhere that a Python index is observable, these break:
- `re.findall('.','é')` → `['é']` (one match, not two)
- `re.findall('.','😀ab')` → `['😀','a','b']`
- `re.findall('.{2}','😀a')` → `['😀a']` — `{2}` counts code points, so an astral char is one
- `re.sub('.','X','é😀')` → `'XX'`
- `re.split('b','😀b😀')` → `['😀','😀']`

**Lone surrogates.** Python strings may contain them; Rust `String` may not.
- `re.findall('.','\ud800')` → `['\ud800']`
- `re.findall('[\ud800-\udfff]','a\ud800b')` → `['\ud800']`

Refuse (at the interpreter level, not the regex level) any subject or pattern string containing an unpaired surrogate — these arrive routinely from `os.listdir` and `surrogateescape` decoding, so this is not theoretical.

---

# 3. Constructs that PARSE cleanly inside the subset but mean something subtly different

These are the dangerous ones: nothing about them looks unsupported, so nothing prompts a refusal. Each is a required differential test.

### 3.1 The empty-match scanning rule (the single most important item)

Since 3.7 the scanner is not "on an empty match, advance one." It is: **after a zero-width match at position p, retry at the same p requiring a non-empty match; only if that fails, advance to p+1.** Everything below falls out of that one rule, and an engine that implements "advance one" gets all of them wrong.

- `re.findall('x*','axbc')` → `['','x','','','']`
- `re.sub('x*','-','abxd')` → `'-a-b--d-'` (the doubled `--` after the `x` is the whole rule in one character)
- `re.sub('','-','ab')` → `'-a-b-'`
- `re.sub('a*','-','aaa')` → `'--'` and `re.subn('a*','-','aaa')` → `('--', 2)`
- `re.findall('a*','aaa')` → `['aaa','']`
- `re.findall(r'\d*','1a2')` → `['1','','2','']`
- `re.sub(r'\d*','-','a1b')` → `'-a--b-'`
- `re.sub(r'\b','|','ab cd')` → `'|ab| |cd|'`
- `re.findall('(?:)','ab')` → `['','','']`
- `re.findall('a{0}','b')` → `['','']`
- `re.findall('x*','')` → `['']`, `re.sub('x*','y','')` → `'y'`, `re.subn('','X','')` → `('X', 1)`

And the lazy case, which is where "advance one" produces output that is not merely differently-punctuated but has *lost characters*:

- `re.findall('a*?','aaa')` → `['','a','','a','','a','']` (7 items)
- **`re.sub('a*?','-','aa')` → `'-----'`** — five dashes and no `a` survives. A naive engine gives `'-a-a-'`.
- `re.split('a*?','abc')` → `['','','','b','c','']`

### 3.2 `split` and `findall` disagree about unmatched groups: `''` vs `None`

- `re.findall(r'(a)(b)?','ab a')` → `[('a','b'), ('a','')]` — empty string
- `re.findall(r'(a)*','b')` → `['','']`
- `re.findall(r'(a)(?:(b)|(c))','ab ac')` → `[('a','b',''), ('a','','c')]`
- `re.split(r'(a)|(b)','xaybz')` → `['x','a',None,'y',None,'b','z']` — **None**
- `re.split(r'(x)*','abc')` → `['',None,'a',None,'b',None,'c',None,'']`
- `re.split('(a)(b)?','a')` → `['','a',None,'']`

Same underlying "group did not participate," two different renderings. Also: `findall` returns a flat list of strings for 0 or 1 groups and a list of tuples for ≥2 — `re.findall(r'(a)','aa')` → `['a','a']`, not `[('a',),('a',)]`.

### 3.3 `split` emits captured groups, and interacts with 3.1

- `re.split(r'(\W)','a,b;c')` → `['a',',','b',';','c']`
- `re.split(r'\b','a b')` → `['','a',' ','b','']`
- `re.split('x*','axbxc')` → `['','a','','b','','c','']`
- `re.split('','abc')` → `['','a','b','c','']`
- `re.split('|','abc')` → `['','a','b','c','']` — an empty alternation branch, not a literal pipe
- `re.split('$','ab\n')` → `['ab','\n','']`
- **`re.split('x*','axbxc',1)` → `['','axbxc']`** — maxsplit=1 spends its one split on the *empty* match at position 0. `re.split('x*','axbxc',2)` → `['','a','bxc']`.

### 3.4 Capture groups retain the last iteration; they are not reset per repetition

- `re.findall(r'(a|b)+','ab')` → `['b']`
- `re.findall(r'(?:(a)|(b))+','ab')` → `[('a','b')]` — group 1 keeps `'a'` from an earlier iteration even though the last iteration took the `(b)` branch. Engines that clear group slots on entry to each repetition give `('','b')`.
- `re.findall(r'(a|b)*?c','abc')` → `['b']`
- **`re.findall(r'(a?)*','aa')` → `['','']`** — the overall match consumes `'aa'` but group 1 is `''`, because the repeat's terminating iteration matched empty and overwrote the slot.

### 3.5 The empty-body-repeat termination rule

`(a*)*` must not loop forever; CPython breaks the repeat when an iteration matches empty.
- `re.findall(r'(a*)*','b')` → `['','']`
- `re.findall(r'(a*)+','b')` → `['','']`

### 3.6 Leftmost-first alternation, not leftmost-longest

- `re.findall('a|ab','ab')` → `['a']`
- `re.findall('(?:a|ab)','ab')` → `['a']`
- `re.findall('(?:ab|a)(?:c|bc)','abc')` → `['abc']` — the first branch's preference is overridden by backtracking, so a "first match wins, no backtrack" shortcut gives `[]`

Any DFA-ish or longest-match optimization is a silent-wrongness generator here.

### 3.7 `$`, `\Z`, and the trailing newline

`$` matches at end of string **and** immediately before a single trailing `\n` — but not before `\r\n` as a unit.
- `re.sub('$','X','ab\n')` → `'abX\nX'`
- `re.sub('$','X','ab')` → `'abX'`
- `re.sub('$','X','a\n\n')` → `'a\nX\nX'` (only one trailing newline is special)
- `re.findall('$','ab\n')` → `['','']`
- `re.findall(r'\Z','ab\n')` → `['']`
- `re.findall('$','')` → `['']`, `re.findall(r'\Z','')` → `['']`
- `re.findall('.$','a\r\n')` → `['\r']`
- **`re.findall('.*$','ab\n')` → `['ab','','']`** — three matches, from 3.1 plus the `$`-before-final-newline rule
- `re.findall('^$','\n')` → `['']`
- `re.findall(r'\b','')` → `[]` (no boundary in an empty string)
- `re.sub(r'\B','-','abc')` → `'a-b-c'`

`.` excludes only `\n` — not `\r`, not U+2028: `re.findall('.','a\nb')` → `['a','b']`, `re.findall('.','a\u2028b')` → 3 matches.

### 3.8 Character-class parsing traps

- **`[]]` is legal and means the set `{']'}`.** `re.findall('[]a]','xa]')` → `['a',']']`; `re.findall('[]]','a]')` → `[']']`; `re.findall('[^]a]','xa]')` → `['x']`. A leading `]` (also right after `^`) is a literal. But `re.findall('[]','a')` → `re.error: unterminated character set at position 0`.
- **`[\b]` is backspace.** `re.findall(r'[\b]','a\bb')` → `['\x08']`. An engine that reuses the word-boundary handler inside classes is silently wrong.
- `re.findall('[a-]','a-')` → `['a','-']`, `re.findall('[-a]','a-')` → `['a','-']`, `re.findall(r'[\w-]','a-')` → `['a','-']` — trailing/leading `-` is a literal, and a `-` after a class escape is a literal.
- `re.findall(r'[\d-z]','a')` → `re.error: bad character range \d-z at position 1`; `re.findall('[z-a]','a')` → `re.error: bad character range z-a at position 1`.
- `re.findall('[\\w[]','a[')` → `['a','[']` — a bare `[` inside a class is a literal.
- **The FutureWarning family — refuse these outright.** They parse, they match, and they print to stderr, which the exit-90 contract has no room for:
